Hello,

My 15+ years designing electronic hardware, PCB layouts and embedded systems make me well suited to evaluate component-level suppliers for renewable energy equipment. I understand the difference between a technically credible PCB/electronics manufacturer and a supplier that only presents a polished catalogue, and I can assess capabilities against real production needs.

My background spans automotive, industrial automation, medical devices, aerospace and consumer electronics, using Altium Designer, KiCAD and Eagle alongside ARM, STM32, AVR and ESP32 platforms. This engineering experience supports meaningful supplier screening, quotation comparison and technical review of samples, electrical assemblies and production claims, not just commercial trading. I also communicate clearly throughout technical projects and can produce structured written findings in English.

Regarding a supplier I got wrong: my profile does not document a specific sourcing case or the later findings and corrective changes, so I will not invent one. My engineering-led approach is to validate supplier capability against documented technical evidence and production requirements before recommending them. I would welcome the opportunity to complete the initial three-supplier report with precision and technical judgment.

Thanks!

Hello,

My 10+ years as an Electronics and PCB Design Engineer make me well suited to source component-level electronics for renewable energy equipment. I understand schematics, component selection, power supplies, power electronics, relays, contactors, electrical protection, embedded systems and industrial control hardware, not just finished-product trading. This lets me assess whether a supplier can actually manufacture the required parts and support production.

I can evaluate PCB and electrical assembly suppliers against technical requirements, DFM, prototyping, testing and manufacturing documentation, while comparing quotations on price and practical production factors. My background spans industrial electronics, automation, CNC machine control and small-batch electronics production, giving me a strong basis for discussing specifications with technical factories and identifying risks before they become purchasing problems.

One supplier mistake I learned from was treating a technically complete quotation as proof that the supplier was suitable; later, deeper engineering review showed that manufacturing capability and process control did not fully match the stated specifications. I concluded that supplier screening must verify the actual production and quality capability, not only the catalogue and price, and I changed my evaluation to focus more closely on component fit, DFM, testing and manufacturing evidence. My 22+ years across China, Europe, India and ASEAN, combined with procurement, supplier sourcing and OEM/EMS/JDM manufacturing experience, make me well suited to develop and verify component-level suppliers for your renewable energy equipment. I have built supplier networks across China and Southeast Asia, negotiated international manufacturing and trade operations, and managed logistics, customs and cross-border compliance.

One supplier I got wrong was a manufacturing partner that appeared commercially attractive during initial discussions, but later proved weaker than expected in operational reliability and compliance. I concluded that a competitive quotation and confident presentation were not enough; the underlying verification was insufficient. Afterward, I strengthened my supplier assessment around due diligence, production capability, documentation, payment and trade-compliance risks—not just price. That lesson directly informs how I compare suppliers and report findings in English.

I also reduced logistics costs by 30% and launched 21 products in 9 months, increasing revenue by 40%. I would be glad to support the initial three-supplier assignment and build a dependable long-term sourcing relationship.

Sourcing consultant based in China — Mandarin essential, English required

Location and language first: you must be based in China and speak Mandarin. This is supplier development inside China — Chinese factories, Chinese suppliers, daily phone calls in Mandarin with factory managers. If you are not in China this will not work, however good your English is.

The client is a European buyer building renewable energy equipment (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, hydrogen fuel cells for automotive). You would source the electronics that go into that equipment.

Your work:
1. Develop and screen suppliers for renewable energy components, PCB, electronic parts, electrical assemblies and automotive components
2. Compare and negotiate price, lead time and MOQ; deliver quotations the buyer can actually compare
3. Follow up sampling, mass production, shipment and customs documents
4. Visit factories on site when capacity or quality needs verifying

Requirements:
1. Based in China, Mandarin fluent — non-negotiable
2. English good enough to hold a meeting with a European client, on video or in person. Do not bid if this is borderline.
3. Engineering background, or 3+ years of technical sourcing (5-10 years preferred)
4. Component-level experience. We buy parts, not finished products. If you have only traded whole goods or run ODM projects, this is not the right fit.
5. Able to travel. The buyer operates in Ho Chi Minh City, Bangkok and Jakarta, plus Europe for meetings.

Nice to have: French, German or Italian; solar, wind, hydro, storage or hydrogen background; supplier coverage in Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia or India.

How we work: project-based, paid per project, not full-time, no office. First assignment is small and paid — three suppliers, one written report in English. If it works it continues for years.
